data.name: Help_QuickTip_Body
data.value: Press F1 anywhere in the app to open this Help Center instantly. Zephyr's Elixir is designed to be learned in minutes, not weeks — take your time.

data.name: Help_Welcome_Intro1
data.value: It's good to have you here. Zephyr's Elixir was built around a simple question:

data.name: Help_Welcome_Intro_Emphasis
data.value: why can't Android optimization feel as refined as the devices it runs on?

data.name: Help_Welcome_Intro2
data.value: What you're looking at isn't another bare command-line frontend. It's a carefully crafted optimization suite that hides raw ADB power behind a calm, elegant interface — and treats your device with the respect it deserves.

data.name: Help_Welcome_Power_Body
data.value: The main Optimize button runs a seven-stage pipeline — cache cleanup, memory triage, deep storage clean, network tuning, system tuning, package compilation, and DEX optimization — orchestrated through 120 tracked steps. You press one button; the app handles the rest.

data.name: Help_Welcome_Transparency_Body
data.value: Every ADB command is streamed live to the Optimization Console as it runs. No black box: you always see exactly what is being sent to your device, in the order it's being sent.

data.name: Help_Welcome_Reversibility_Body
data.value: Changes made in the Advanced section are tracked individually. Animation scales, private DNS, compilation mode, spoofed battery level — each has a dedicated Reset button, and a single Reset All brings everything back to the factory defaults Android ships with.

data.name: Help_Welcome_NoRoot_Body
data.value: Zephyr's Elixir speaks only through ADB (Android Debug Bridge). No magisk, no custom recovery, no tripped warranty. Enable USB debugging and you're ready — nothing else changes about how your device was sold to you.

data.name: Help_Welcome_Privacy_Body
data.value: The app works entirely on your machine. No account, no analytics, no background telemetry. The only network calls made are for license validation (if you activate Pro) and for optional cloud package intelligence when you open app details in the Debloat screen.

data.name: Help_Welcome_Philosophy1
data.value: Optimization shouldn't feel like homework. You shouldn't need to memorize shell commands, chase outdated forum threads, or guess which package is safe to disable. Good software does the reading for you and shows its work.

data.name: Help_Welcome_Philosophy2
data.value: That's the promise behind every detail here — the live particle field on the Optimize page, the real-time battery readout in the sidebar, the soft glow behind each action card. Nothing is decorative for its own sake: each element exists to make the underlying engineering feel approachable.

data.name: Help_Welcome_Ready_Body
data.value: Open First Steps if you've never enabled USB debugging before. Jump to Quick Guide if you just want to optimize and get on with your day. This guide stays one keystroke away — F1, whenever you need it.

data.name: Help_FirstSteps_Intro
data.value: Before Zephyr's Elixir can talk to your phone, your phone needs to know it's allowed to listen. This takes about two minutes and only has to be done once per device.

data.name: Help_FirstSteps_USB_Body
data.value: USB debugging is a built-in developer mode that lets a trusted computer send ADB commands to the device. It's part of vanilla Android — no modification, no risk.

data.name: Help_FirstSteps_Step2
data.value: 2. Scroll down and tap About phone.

data.name: Help_FirstSteps_Step3
data.value: 3. Find Build number. On some skins it's under Software information.

data.name: Help_FirstSteps_Step4
data.value: 4. Tap Build number seven times. Enter your PIN if asked. You'll see "You are now a developer!".

data.name: Help_FirstSteps_Step5
data.value: 5. Go back to Settings and open the new Developer options entry (usually under System).

data.name: Help_FirstSteps_Step6
data.value: 6. Turn on USB debugging. Accept the warning dialog.

data.name: Help_FirstSteps_Step7
data.value: 7. Optional but recommended: also turn on Stay awake, so the screen doesn't sleep while you're working.

data.name: Help_FirstSteps_Connect_Body
data.value: Plug your phone into the PC with the cable that came in the box, or any certified data cable. Cheap charge-only cables are the single most common reason the device doesn't show up.

data.name: Help_FirstSteps_Cable_Body
data.value: If the device charges but Zephyr's Elixir can't see it, swap the cable before doing anything else. The cable that shipped with your phone always works; thin aftermarket cables often only carry power.

data.name: Help_FirstSteps_FirstConnect
data.value: The first time you connect, Android will ask you to confirm the pairing:

data.name: Help_FirstSteps_Popup1
data.value: • A dialog titled "Allow USB debugging?" appears on the phone.

data.name: Help_FirstSteps_Popup2
data.value: • Tick "Always allow from this computer" so you don't see it every time.

data.name: Help_FirstSteps_Verify_Body
data.value: Zephyr's Elixir constantly watches for devices in the background. The sidebar at the left is the source of truth:

data.name: Help_FirstSteps_Verify1
data.value: • Connected: the model name appears under the device icon, and a live battery bar fills up.

data.name: Help_FirstSteps_Verify2
data.value: • Not connected: you see a muted "No device connected" message and action buttons stay disabled.

data.name: Help_FirstSteps_VerifyHint
data.value: If the sidebar still says No device after a few seconds, open the Troubleshooting section — the first entry, Device not detected, covers every known cause.

data.name: Help_FirstSteps_Wireless_Body
data.value: Once the first USB handshake is done, Android 11 and newer can keep the ADB session running over Wi-Fi. No cable required from then on.

data.name: Help_FirstSteps_WStep1
data.value: 1. Make sure the phone and PC are on the same Wi-Fi network.

data.name: Help_FirstSteps_WStep2
data.value: 2. On the phone, open Developer options and enable Wireless debugging.

data.name: Help_FirstSteps_WStep3
data.value: 3. Tap "Pair device with pairing code" — you'll see an IP address, a port, and a six-digit code.

data.name: Help_FirstSteps_WStep4
data.value: 4. On Home in Zephyr's Elixir, click Wireless connection and paste the three values.

data.name: Help_FirstSteps_WStep5
data.value: 5. The app handles pairing, connection, and verification. The cable becomes optional.

data.name: Help_FirstSteps_AllSet_Body
data.value: Everything Zephyr's Elixir can do is now unlocked for this device. When you're ready for a guided first run, jump to the Quick Guide — four steps, under three minutes.

data.name: Help_Basics_Intro
data.value: A quick orientation to what's running under the hood and how the interface maps to it. This section is worth reading once — everything else in the app will make more sense afterwards.

data.name: Help_Basics_ADB_Body
data.value: ADB stands for Android Debug Bridge. It's the official developer protocol Google ships inside Android itself — the same tool used by app developers, manufacturers, and Google's own engineering teams. Zephyr's Elixir bundles a signed copy of the ADB platform-tools and never touches system files directly.

data.name: Help_Basics_ADB_Safe1
data.value: • It's Google's own protocol — not a hack, not a patched binary.

data.name: Help_Basics_ADB_Safe2
data.value: • It runs inside Android's existing permission sandbox. No root, no bootloader unlock, no warranty flag.

data.name: Help_Basics_ADB_Safe3
data.value: • Every command that reaches your device is shown in the Optimization Console first.

data.name: Help_Basics_ADB_Safe4
data.value: • Any setting the app changes can be reverted from the Advanced screen with one click.

data.name: Help_Basics_Sidebar_Body
data.value: The dark rail on the left is your navigation. Seven entries, always visible:

data.name: Help_Basics_Sidebar_Home
data.value: • Home — landing page, quick actions, device status.

data.name: Help_Basics_Sidebar_Optimize
data.value: • Optimize — the full seven-stage performance pipeline.

data.name: Help_Basics_Sidebar_Debloat
data.value: • Debloat — list, disable, uninstall and review user or system apps.

data.name: Help_Basics_Sidebar_Advanced
data.value: • Advanced — granular tuning: private DNS, animation scales, compilation mode, and more.

data.name: Help_Basics_Sidebar_Settings
data.value: • Settings — language, ADB status, diagnostic log export, license management.

data.name: Help_Basics_Sidebar_Help
data.value: • Help — where you are right now. F1 brings you back any time.

data.name: Help_Basics_Sidebar_Device
data.value: At the bottom of the sidebar sits the live device card: model name and battery level, updated in real time. It's the fastest way to confirm the connection without leaving the current page.

data.name: Help_Basics_Console_Body
data.value: On the Optimize page, the dark panel at the right is the Console. Every ADB command Zephyr's Elixir sends is logged there, with timestamps and output. It's the same stream you'd see in a terminal — just prettier.

data.name: Help_Basics_Console_Tip_Body
data.value: If something ever behaves unexpectedly, the Console is always the first place to look. You can export the full diagnostic log from Settings → Export logs at any time.

data.name: Help_Basics_HowOpt_Body
data.value: A single Optimize run walks through seven real stages, each touching a different subsystem. You'll see the stage name update live as it progresses:

data.name: Help_Basics_Cat_Performance_Body
data.value: Clears app caches iteratively, trims memory pressure, frees storage, and force-compiles installed packages in speed mode so cold starts feel snappier.

data.name: Help_Basics_Cat_Battery_Body
data.value: Applies stricter standby bucket policies, enables adaptive battery management, and tones down window, transition and animator durations — small changes, real time-on-battery gains.

data.name: Help_Basics_Cat_Network_Body
data.value: Stops constant Wi-Fi and BLE background scans, tunes the DNS resolver, and primes the network stack so web pages and API calls resolve faster.

data.name: Help_Basics_Cat_Privacy_Body
data.value: Reduces background chatter from ad-tracking libraries, tightens captive portal probes, and — with the Pro module loaded — zeroes out the advertising ID and disables Android Safety Core scanning.

data.name: Help_Basics_Extreme_Body
data.value: Standard optimization is what runs by default and is designed to be safe on every supported device. Extreme mode — exposed via the toggle on the Optimize page — goes further: it kill-alls background services, trims caches aggressively, force-compiles packages with the speed profile, and turns animations down to half speed. Extreme is a Pro-only feature and only activates when the Pro module is loaded.

data.name: Help_Basics_Extreme_Hint_Body
data.value: After an Extreme run, a full reboot is recommended so Android can rebuild its package caches cleanly. Everything is still fully reversible from the Advanced screen.

data.name: Help_Basics_Safety_Body
data.value: Android is resilient. Nothing Zephyr's Elixir does requires root, so there's no partition to brick and no bootloop risk. That said, if you ever feel an app is misbehaving after an optimization run:

data.name: Help_Basics_Safety_IfWrong
data.value: Recovery, in order of how much you want to undo:

data.name: Help_Basics_Safety_Step1
data.value: 1. Reboot the device. Most of what Optimize touches settles cleanly after one restart.

data.name: Help_Basics_Safety_Step2
data.value: 2. Open Advanced and press Reset on the specific setting that's bothering you (DNS, animations, compilation, etc).

data.name: Help_Basics_Safety_Step3
data.value: 3. Still not right? Hit Reset All in Advanced — this walks back every change Zephyr's Elixir ever made to this device.

data.name: Help_Basics_Safety_Restore
data.value: For apps that were disabled in Debloat, the History tab keeps a record of every uninstall and lets you reinstall them at any time.

data.name: Help_Quick_Intro
data.value: Four steps. Roughly three minutes. This is the shortest path from "just installed" to "noticeably faster device".

data.name: Help_Quick_Step1_Body1
data.value: Plug in the USB cable and confirm the Allow USB debugging prompt on the phone. If you prefer wireless, click Wireless connection on the Home page and follow the short pairing flow.

data.name: Help_Quick_Step1_Body2
data.value: Confirmation lives in the sidebar: when the model name replaces "No device connected" and the battery bar lights up, you're good to go.

data.name: Help_Quick_Step2_Body1
data.value: From Home, click Start optimization — or open the Optimize screen directly from the sidebar and press the large button there.

data.name: Help_Quick_Step2_Body2
data.value: Have a Pro license? You can also flip the Extreme toggle before starting for a deeper pass.

data.name: Help_Quick_Step3_Body1
data.value: The progress ring climbs through 120 steps while the Console streams every command in real time. An on-screen timer tracks total run time.

data.name: Help_Quick_Step3_Body2
data.value: You can cancel at any point with Stop. Partial progress is already applied and always safe.

data.name: Help_Quick_Step4_Body1
data.value: When the run completes, the report card summarizes what changed. A reboot is optional for standard mode but recommended after Extreme, so the system can rebuild package caches.

data.name: Help_Quick_Step4_Body2
data.value: That's the whole loop. Come back and run it again whenever the device starts feeling sluggish — there's no harm in repeating.

data.name: Help_Quick_Next_Body
data.value: Open Debloat to strip out apps you never use. Open Advanced to dial in private DNS, animation speed, or — on Pro — shut down the more opinionated parts of Google Play Services. The Complete Guide walks through every screen in detail.

data.name: Help_Guide_Intro
data.value: A walkthrough of every screen in Zephyr's Elixir, in the order they appear in the sidebar. Read top to bottom, or jump to the section you care about.

data.name: Help_Guide_Home_Body
data.value: Your landing page. Version number, app changelog shortcut, and the two primary actions every user needs.

data.name: Help_Guide_Home_Optimize_Body
data.value: Jumps straight to the Optimize screen and kicks off a full standard run. This button is disabled until a device is connected — the tooltip will tell you so.

data.name: Help_Guide_Home_Wireless_Body
data.value: Opens the guided wireless ADB pairing dialog. Enter the IP, port, and six-digit code from Developer options → Wireless debugging and Zephyr's Elixir handles the rest.

data.name: Help_Guide_Home_Wireless_Req
data.value: Requires Android 11 or newer on the device and the PC to be on the same network.

data.name: Help_Guide_Home_Changelog_Body
data.value: A link under the version number opens the full changelog dialog with every change since the previous release.

data.name: Help_Guide_Optimize_Body
data.value: The main performance workshop. One primary action, a progress ring, a live timer, and the full Optimization Console.

data.name: Help_Guide_Optimize_Process_Body
data.value: Every run walks through the same seven stages, in order, across 120 tracked steps:

data.name: Help_Guide_Optimize_Cat1
data.value: 1. Cache cleanup — iterative clearing of app and system caches.

data.name: Help_Guide_Optimize_Cat2
data.value: 2. Memory management — identifies heavy foreground apps and trims runaway memory.

data.name: Help_Guide_Optimize_Cat3
data.value: 3. Deep storage clean — removes stale temporary files the OS normally hangs onto.

data.name: Help_Guide_Optimize_Cat4
data.value: 4. Network tuning — DNS resolver warm-up and background scan throttling.

data.name: Help_Guide_Optimize_Cat5
data.value: 5. System tuning, package compilation, and DEX optimization — the final three stages that re-tune scheduler hints and force-compile installed packages so cold starts feel faster.

data.name: Help_Guide_Extreme_Body
data.value: The Extreme toggle unlocks a more aggressive pass: background services are killed outright, caches are trimmed up to 1 TB worth of slack space, system packages are force-compiled in speed profile, and animation scales are pushed to 0.5×. Cached apps freezer and multi-core packet scheduler are enabled where the hardware supports them.

data.name: Help_Guide_Extreme_Note
data.value: Extreme requires an active Pro license and the Pro module loaded. Without both, the toggle stays disabled and shows an upgrade hint on hover.

data.name: Help_Guide_Monitoring_Body
data.value: Four live indicators keep you informed while the pipeline runs:

data.name: Help_Guide_Monitoring_Progress
data.value: • A progress ring filling from 0 to 120 steps.

data.name: Help_Guide_Monitoring_Timer
data.value: • A total-elapsed timer, updated every second.

data.name: Help_Guide_Monitoring_Console
data.value: • The Console, streaming each ADB command and its output in real time.

data.name: Help_Guide_Monitoring_Device
data.value: • The sidebar device card, confirming the phone is still connected and reporting battery level.

data.name: Help_Guide_Optimize_Hint_Body
data.value: If the device disconnects mid-run, Zephyr's Elixir cancels the pipeline automatically and keeps partial progress. You can safely re-run from scratch.

data.name: Help_Guide_Debloat_Body
data.value: Where you reclaim space and attention. Enumerates every package on the device, groups user vs system apps, and lets you disable or uninstall them cleanly.

data.name: Help_Guide_Debloat_Load_Body
data.value: The Load apps button queries the device for installed packages, pulls each icon asynchronously, and sorts the list alphabetically. Icons stream in as they arrive — no need to wait for the whole list before scrolling.

data.name: Help_Guide_Debloat_Filter_Body
data.value: The filter tabs split apps by type: User, System, or Disabled. A free-text search bar narrows results by name or package. Tick the checkboxes to build a multi-selection — the count in the header updates live.

data.name: Help_Guide_Debloat_Actions_Body
data.value: With apps selected, three actions are available: Disable (pm disable-user) keeps the APK on disk but stops the app from running, Uninstall (pm uninstall --user 0) removes it for the current user, and Manage opens a details panel with permissions, standby bucket, and cloud-powered safety analysis.

data.name: Help_Guide_Debloat_Hint_Body
data.value: Every uninstall is logged with its package name, version, icon, and timestamp. Reinstalling is one click — on Pro, APKs are backed up locally first, so you can reinstall later even if the device is offline.

data.name: Help_Guide_Advanced_Body
data.value: Individual, fine-grained knobs. Every setting here has its own Reset button, and there's a Reset All at the top that rewinds every change you've ever made through the app.

data.name: Help_Guide_DNS_Body
data.value: Pick from five curated providers — NextDNS, AdGuard, Cloudflare, Google, Quad9 — or type your own hostname. Zephyr's Elixir live-pings each choice in the dropdown so you can see real latency before you commit. Apply sets Android's private_dns_mode to hostname and writes the chosen provider.

data.name: Help_Guide_Animation_Body
data.value: A single slider drives all three global animation scales (window, transition, animator duration) in lockstep. Drag it toward 0 for a UI that feels instant, or back to 1.0 for the stock Android feel.

data.name: Help_Guide_ResetAll_Body
data.value: One button, full rewind. Every DNS override, animation tweak, compilation setting, spoofed battery value, and Pro-only privacy change goes back to Android defaults. The app shows a confirmation dialog before doing anything destructive.

data.name: Help_Guide_Settings_App_Body
data.value: Language (English / Italian, switch live with no restart), automatic update checks, and the Reset to defaults helper.

data.name: Help_Guide_Settings_Device_Body
data.value: The ADB status card confirms the bundled ADB executable is valid. Export logs writes the full diagnostic log to a file you choose — handy if you ever want to share a run with someone else.

data.name: Help_Guide_Settings_Legal_Body
data.value: Opens the full license text, the privacy policy, and the Pro activation dialog. Activation uses a Z-prefixed key (format Z-XXXXXX-XXXXXXXX-XXXXXXX) purchased from the official store.

data.name: Help_Guide_Explore_Body
data.value: Tools (the sidebar's fourth entry) hosts the APK Installer, the Power Menu for reboots and fastboot/recovery entry, and — on Pro — the low-latency Screen Mirror. It's worth a visit after you've gotten comfortable with the main screens.

data.name: Help_Trouble_Intro
data.value: The short list of things that can go wrong, and the fixes that solve almost all of them. If your issue isn't covered here, the Settings → Export logs button turns your current session into a shareable text file.

data.name: Help_Trouble_NotDetected_Body
data.value: By far the most common issue, and almost always one of four causes. Work through them in order: 1) swap the USB cable — charge-only cables are the usual culprit. 2) re-check that USB debugging is still on under Developer options. 3) on the phone, accept the Allow USB debugging prompt and tick Always allow. 4) try a different USB port on the PC, preferably one directly on the motherboard rather than on a hub.

data.name: Help_Trouble_WirelessFail_Body
data.value: Confirm both devices are on the same Wi-Fi network (not a guest network or a VPN). The six-digit code expires after about a minute — generate a fresh one from the phone's Wireless debugging screen and try again. Corporate networks sometimes block the mDNS traffic ADB uses; a personal hotspot is a reliable fallback.

data.name: Help_Trouble_Stuck_Body
data.value: Look at the Console: if it's still scrolling, the run is fine — some stages (like package compilation) simply take longer on devices with many installed apps. If the Console hasn't moved in more than a minute, press Stop, reboot the device, and start a fresh run.

data.name: Help_Trouble_Strange_Body
data.value: Reboot first — Android often just needs to rebuild caches. If the issue persists, clear that single app's cache and storage from Android Settings → Apps. Nothing Zephyr's Elixir does damages the app itself; clearing its own cache will always recover it.

data.name: Help_Trouble_AppsEmpty_Body
data.value: Press Load apps again. If the list still doesn't populate, the device is likely disconnected or sleeping — wake the screen and confirm the sidebar still shows the device name. A successful load always logs the package count in the console at the top of the panel.

data.name: Help_Trouble_DisabledCritical_Title
data.value: I disabled something I shouldn't have

data.name: Help_Trouble_DisabledCritical_Body
data.value: Open the History tab in Debloat and hit Reinstall on the affected package. Disabled apps are never actually removed — pm enable is one click away. The cloud safety analysis flags packages tagged as Critical up front, exactly to prevent this situation.

data.name: Help_Trouble_DNS_Body
data.value: Some carriers override DNS on mobile data — toggle Wi-Fi on to confirm the setting took effect. If a hostname won't resolve, Zephyr's Elixir will show the error inline. Press Reset on the DNS card to clear private_dns_mode and return to the carrier default.

data.name: Help_Trouble_AnimSlider_Body
data.value: The slider is disabled whenever no device is connected — the sidebar will confirm this. Reconnect and it becomes interactive immediately; live sync runs automatically.

data.name: Help_Trouble_ExportLogs_Body
data.value: From Settings → Export logs, save the full session log to a text file. It contains every ADB command and response Zephyr's Elixir has issued — enough context to reproduce almost any issue.

data.name: Help_Trouble_Reset_Body
data.value: Advanced → Reset All undoes every change Zephyr's Elixir has ever applied to this device. It's the nuclear option, and it's completely safe — all it does is restore Android's out-of-box defaults for the settings the app touches.

data.name: Help_Trouble_StillNeed_Body
data.value: Open Settings → Export logs, attach the generated file, and reach out through the official website or GitHub issue tracker. Pro users get priority triage under the bundled support channel.

data.name: Help_Tips_Intro
data.value: Small details that make a big difference once you know them. Scan this page once — you'll recognize these moments later.

data.name: Help_Tips_Shortcut_Body
data.value: F1 — anywhere, any screen, any moment. That's the only one you need.

data.name: Help_Tip_Shortcut_Body
data.value: From anywhere in Zephyr's Elixir, a single F1 tap brings you back here. No menu diving, no context switching.

data.name: Help_Tip_Performance_Body
data.value: There's no harm in running the pipeline as often as you like, but once a month is enough for most people. Running it after large OS updates is especially worthwhile — the package compiler gets a fresh pass at the newly-installed binaries.

data.name: Help_Tip_Battery_Body
data.value: The sidebar battery indicator isn't decoration — it refreshes live from the device. Use it as a glanceable sanity check that the connection is still healthy, without leaving the current page.

data.name: Help_Tip_Console_Body
data.value: Every command, every response, timestamped. The Console is both your live status display and your first debugging tool. When something feels wrong, look there before anywhere else.

data.name: Help_Tip_Backup_Body
data.value: The History tab inside Debloat records every uninstall with its package name, version, icon, and timestamp. A single click reinstalls. Pro users also get the original APK backed up locally, so reinstallation works even when the Play Store doesn't.

data.name: Help_Tip_Wireless_Body
data.value: Once the initial USB pairing is done, Wireless debugging means you never have to plug in again. The Wireless connection dialog on Home is the quickest way to pair.

data.name: Help_Tip_Safety_Body
data.value: Every operation Zephyr's Elixir performs is individually reversible. Worst case, Advanced → Reset All returns the device to defaults. You have room to experiment.

data.name: Help_Tip_Pro_Title
data.value: Pro is an unlock, not a rewrite

data.name: Help_Tip_Pro_Body
data.value: Free already ships the complete seven-stage Optimize pipeline, full Debloat, wireless ADB, private DNS, animation tuning, APK installer, and the power menu. Pro adds Extreme optimization, Screen Mirror, multi-APK install, APK local backup, unlimited cloud safety analysis, and the privacy pack (Safety Core, Ad ID reset, captive portal off, Google Core Control, virtual RAM off). Same app, deeper knobs.

data.name: Help_Faq_Intro
data.value: Everything people usually ask before, during, and after their first run. Use the search box below to jump straight to a topic.

data.name: Help_Faq_Safe_Q
data.value: Is Zephyr's Elixir safe to use?

data.name: Help_Faq_Safe_A
data.value: Yes. Every action runs through official ADB commands inside Android's own permission sandbox — no root, no bootloader unlock, no modifications to system partitions. Every change is tracked and can be reversed from the Advanced screen at any time.

data.name: Help_Faq_Warranty_A
data.value: No. USB debugging and ADB are official Android features shipped by Google, enabled the same way any user would enable Developer options. Nothing Zephyr's Elixir does trips the factory reset counter or modifies bootloader state.

data.name: Help_Faq_Root_Q
data.value: Do I need root or an unlocked bootloader?

data.name: Help_Faq_Root_A
data.value: Neither. Zephyr's Elixir is designed precisely so you don't have to. If you already happen to be rooted, the app still works — it just doesn't need the extra privileges.

data.name: Help_Faq_AndroidVersions_A
data.value: Android 8 (Oreo) and newer for USB connections. Wireless debugging requires Android 11 or newer, because that's when Google added the pairing-code flow the app uses. Everything in between is fully supported.

data.name: Help_Faq_SystemReq_Q
data.value: What do I need on the PC?

data.name: Help_Faq_SystemReq_A
data.value: Windows 10 (64-bit) or newer, around 200 MB of free disk space, and a free USB port. Zephyr's Elixir runs on .NET 8 and ships with its own signed ADB platform-tools — nothing extra to install.

data.name: Help_Faq_Wireless_A
data.value: Yes, on Android 11 or newer. Open Wireless connection from the Home page, enter the IP, port, and six-digit pairing code shown on the phone, and the app handles the rest. Once paired, the cable becomes optional.

data.name: Help_Faq_NotDetected_Q
data.value: My device isn't detected — what now?

data.name: Help_Faq_NotDetected_A
data.value: In order: swap the cable (charge-only cables are the usual reason), confirm USB debugging is still enabled under Developer options, accept the Allow USB debugging prompt on the phone, and try a different USB port. If none of that helps, Troubleshooting → Device not detected has a deeper walkthrough.

data.name: Help_Faq_WirelessFail_A
data.value: Make sure both devices are on the same Wi-Fi network (not a guest SSID) and that no active VPN is routing traffic off-network. The pairing code expires after roughly a minute — regenerate and try again. Corporate networks sometimes block the mDNS traffic ADB needs; a personal hotspot is a reliable fallback.

data.name: Help_Faq_WhatHappens_Q
data.value: What actually happens when I press Optimize?

data.name: Help_Faq_WhatHappens_A
data.value: A seven-stage pipeline of 120 tracked steps runs: cache cleanup, memory triage, deep storage clean, network tuning, system tuning, package compilation, and DEX optimization. Each stage sends a sequence of standard ADB shell commands, all visible in the Console as they execute.

data.name: Help_Faq_HowOften_Q
data.value: How often should I run it?

data.name: Help_Faq_HowOften_A
data.value: Once a month is plenty for most users. Running it after a major Android update or after installing many new apps gives the package compiler something to work with and tends to show a bigger improvement.

data.name: Help_Faq_Customize_Q
data.value: Can I pick which stages run?

data.name: Help_Faq_Customize_A
data.value: The one-button Optimize is intentionally fixed — it's designed to be safe on every device in that exact order. For granular control, Advanced lets you tweak DNS, animation speed, compilation mode, and battery level independently, with per-setting reset buttons.

data.name: Help_Faq_ExtremeVsStandard_Q
data.value: What's the difference between Standard and Extreme?

data.name: Help_Faq_ExtremeVsStandard_A
data.value: Standard is the default, designed to be safe on every supported device. Extreme — available with the Pro module — adds aggressive background kill, 1 TB cache trim, speed-profile force compile across all packages, half-speed animations, cached apps freezer, and multi-core packet scheduler. A reboot is recommended after Extreme runs.

data.name: Help_Faq_SomethingWrong_Q
data.value: An app misbehaves after a run. What do I do?

data.name: Help_Faq_SomethingWrong_A
data.value: Reboot first — Android typically just needs to rebuild package caches. If a single app is still acting up, clearing its cache from Android Settings → Apps usually resolves it. Nothing Zephyr's Elixir does damages application data.

data.name: Help_Faq_Logs_Q
data.value: Where are the logs and how do I share them?

data.name: Help_Faq_Logs_A
data.value: The live feed is in the Optimization Console on the Optimize page. Settings → Export logs writes the full diagnostic log — every command and response from the current session — to a text file you choose. Attach that file when asking for help.

data.name: Help_Faq_DataCollection_Q
data.value: Does Zephyr's Elixir collect any data?

data.name: Help_Faq_DataCollection_A
data.value: No analytics, no telemetry, no user tracking. The only network traffic the app generates is license validation (if Pro is activated) and optional cloud package safety analysis when you open app details in Debloat. Both flows are documented in the privacy policy under Settings.

data.name: Help_Faq_ProFeatures_A
data.value: Extreme optimization with cached apps freezer and multi-core scheduler, Screen Mirror with low-latency streaming, multi-APK install, local APK backup on every uninstall, unlimited cloud safety analysis (Free is capped at 25 per day), and the privacy pack: Android Safety Core off, advertising ID reset, captive portal disabled, Google Core Control disabled, and per-vendor virtual-RAM disable (Samsung, Xiaomi, OnePlus, Oppo, Vivo, Huawei). Pro is a signed, separately downloaded module — the free app works unchanged without it.

data.name: Help_Faq_ActivatePro_Q
data.value: How do I activate a Pro license?

data.name: Help_Faq_ActivatePro_A
data.value: Open Settings → Pro license. Paste the key you received at purchase (format Z-XXXXXX-XXXXXXXX-XXXXXXX), click Activate, and Zephyr's Elixir downloads the signed Pro module and verifies its public-key token before loading. Activation binds to your device fingerprint and works offline for up to seven days between online re-validations.

data.name: Help_Faq_ApkErrors_Q
data.value: An APK won't install from the APK Installer — why?

data.name: Help_Faq_ApkErrors_A
data.value: Two common causes: the APK's signature conflicts with a version already on the device (uninstall the existing copy first) or the APK's minSdkVersion is higher than the device's Android version. The installer surfaces the exact error message returned by pm install — that message tells you which case you're in.

data.name: Help_About_Intro
data.value: The story behind the app, how it's built, what it stands for, and how to reach the people behind it.

data.name: Help_About_Story1
data.value: Zephyr's Elixir started as a personal itch. Android is a wonderful system buried under a mountain of defaults that rarely suit any given user — and the existing optimization tools either demanded a terminal or looked like they were built by someone who wished they were allowed to use one.

data.name: Help_About_Story2
data.value: The goal was simple: the depth of a shell session, the clarity of a modern design system, and a hard rule that nothing the app does can ever be unfixable. Everything you see here followed from that rule.

data.name: Help_About_Tech_BuiltWith
data.value: • Built on .NET 8 and WPF — native Windows, no web wrapper, no hidden Chromium.

data.name: Help_About_Tech_Architecture
data.value: • Open-core architecture: the free app is the whole product; Pro is a separate, strong-name-signed, AES-GCM-encrypted module loaded through an isolated AssemblyLoadContext.

data.name: Help_About_Tech_UI
data.value: • UI entirely hand-written in XAML with custom glass materials, live particle fields, and full ClearType text rendering — subpixel precision is preserved everywhere no DropShadowEffect sits above a text node.

data.name: Help_About_Tech_Backend
data.value: • Device I/O runs through the official Google ADB platform-tools, bundled and signed with the app. No forked binaries, no reverse-engineered protocols.

data.name: Help_About_Philosophy_Intro
data.value: Four principles that shape every decision:

data.name: Help_About_Phil_Transparent
data.value: • Transparent — every command is visible, every change is logged, every log is exportable.

data.name: Help_About_Phil_Respectful
data.value: • Respectful — your device belongs to you. The app makes suggestions; it never assumes.

data.name: Help_About_Phil_Beautiful
data.value: • Beautiful — a tool you use often should feel good to use. Aesthetics are an engineering concern.

data.name: Help_About_Phil_Empowering
data.value: • Empowering — you should understand more about your device after using the app, not less.

data.name: Help_About_OpenSource_Body
data.value: The free app — the one you're looking at right now — is the complete product for most users. The Pro module is distributed as a separately signed DLL that the app downloads and verifies at runtime: public-key token match, AES-GCM-encrypted at rest, decrypted to a temp file only during load, and wiped afterwards. If the signature doesn't match the expected token, the module is rejected and the app falls back to free mode cleanly. You can inspect the bridge code in the Licensing folder of the project.

data.name: Help_About_License_Body
data.value: The full end-user license agreement and privacy policy are available from Settings → License and Settings → Privacy. Short version: the free tier is free forever, Pro is a paid unlock, and nothing about you is ever sold, profiled, or used for advertising. The technical traffic strictly necessary for license validation and optional cloud safety analysis is fully documented in the privacy policy.
